A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same automotive CFD surrogate research, substantially revised from GP-UPT to AB-UPT. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original GP-UPT benchmarks, volume predictions, drag/lift estimates, transfer-learning experiments and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original AB-UPT benchmarks, architectural ablations, scaling studies, CAD experiments and divergence-free vorticity results, including additional appendix experiments.

M1.justification: v2 replaces GP-UPT's geometry-preserving encoder and auxiliary supernode/field-decoder design with interacting geometry, surface and volume branches. It introduces anchor attention, shared and branch-specific processing, and curl-based vorticity prediction as an architectural constraint (Sections 3.1–3.3). These change the procedure substantially.

E1.justification: ShapeNetCar, AhmedML and DrivAerML remain, but coverage expands to joint surface/volume prediction, including ShapeNetCar volume velocity and high-fidelity vorticity fields. Appendix A.2 adds a DrivAerML scenario with 20% out-of-distribution test samples. DrivAerNet pretraining and cross-fidelity transfer coverage are removed.

E2.justification: The main benchmark adds Graph U-Net, LNO, OFormer and a plain Transformer while removing RegDGCNN (v1 Table 1; v2 Table 4). Appendix A additionally compares against published DoMINO results and k-NN interpolation. Transolver++ is discussed but explicitly excluded from the benchmark.

E3.justification: The reported ShapeNetCar train/test split changes from 800/189 to 789/100. Benchmark training changes from 1000 to 500 epochs, with revised model configurations and precision. v2 introduces 16,384-point surface/volume sampling and chunked benchmark evaluation, plus separate DoMINO and baseline-reproduction protocols. These prevent interpreting cross-version scores as controlled performance gains.

E4.justification: v2 adds systematic architecture ablations (Table 3), training-resolution and overfitting studies (Figure 5), anchor-attention versus interpolation analysis (Table 9), physical-constraint comparisons and baseline reproduction checks. CAD and inference-scaling analyses are revised; v1's optimizer ablation and cross-fidelity transfer study are removed.

E5.justification: v1 does not specify comparable repeated-run reporting. v2 Appendix B.5.3 specifies five training seeds, median performance and averaging over ten evaluation passes; Appendix C additionally reports median and best results. This substantially changes statistical reporting without establishing how many runs were performed for v1.

E6.justification: Benchmark scores are extensively replaced and expanded, with new joint-field, DoMINO and divergence results and removal of transfer results. Drag/lift R2 changes from 0.969/0.971 to 0.963/0.975 under changed models/settings. One v2 result is internally inconsistent: GINO's DrivAerML pressure error is 13.03% in Table 4 but 3.03% in Table 7.

T1.justification: v2 adds a formal anchor-attention definition, computational and memory complexity reasoning, and a curl-based construction guaranteeing divergence-free vorticity. Sections 3.2–3.3 also introduce finite-difference derivatives and normalization corrections. These mathematical constructions and arguments are absent from v1.

C1.justification: v1's central claim of halving high-fidelity data requirements through transfer learning disappears. v2 centers its contribution on problem scale, joint surface/volume prediction beyond 100 million cells, efficient single-GPU training and divergence-free vorticity. CAD independence and accurate drag/lift prediction remain central claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of resolution saturation and overfitting, the accuracy tradeoff from uniform CAD sampling, and quadratic anchor-computation limits. It explicitly distinguishes divergence-free vorticity from incompressible velocity. v1's interpretations concerning transfer-learning data sufficiency and high-frequency prediction errors are removed.

D1.justification: GP-UPT implementation tables and CAD fine-tuning instructions are replaced by extensive AB-UPT branch/anchor configurations, derivative and normalization details, baseline tuning information and EMA settings. v2 also discloses H100 training time/memory and explicit baseline implementation links (Appendix B). These document the revised implementation rather than merely rename it.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around hard physical constraints and scalable CFD surrogates, adding discussion of PINNs, neural conservation laws, Transolver++, DoMINO and GOAT. Existing neural-operator material is partly reorganized, but the new literature and arguments broaden the substantive relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: The title, model terminology and authorship change, while the introduction, method narrative and conclusion are extensively rewritten around problem scale. Experiments are reorganized, dedicated related-work and limitations sections appear, and appendices A–E are restructured into extended results, experimental setup and baseline fairness.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. Architecture diagrams are redrawn, benchmark tables gain new structures and color coding, and extensive scaling plots and ablation tables are added. v1's detailed CFD comparison, transfer-learning and CAD-remeshing displays are removed or replaced.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's limited component validation and unspecified repeated-run reporting, v2 provides systematic architectural ablations, explicit multi-seed evaluation and baseline reproduction checks, substantially strengthening its methodological support. The vorticity construction connects a physical constraint to derivation and experiment. These gains outweigh the removed transfer-learning study, although the conflicting GINO entries in Tables 4 and 7 weaken the universal performance claim.
